chapter: Later views and life in Dallas
title: The Jo Jones cymbal story about Parker
summary: The interviewer tells of Jo Jones throwing a cymbal at Parker's jam; Smith never heard it.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: You've probably heard the famous story that when Charlie Parker was starting out to play he went to one of these jam sessions and tried to get in with sort of the big company, and he didn't do very well. And there's a story that Jo Jones unscrewed his cymbal and threw it on the floor.
Were you there when that happened?
No. Where did that happen at?
Somewhere in Kansas City. One of the clubs where there was a big jam session going on, and Charlie Parker tried to make it and couldn't. Jo Jones was disgusted with what he was doing...
...and he took off his top cymbal and threw it on the floor.
No. No, I didn't hear that. No, I sure didn't.
That would have been early on, though -- I mean in 1934, 1935.

Because Charile's supposed to have gone off to the Ozarks that next summer, I think with George Lee or one of the bands, and there was nothing to do but study there. So he really learned all of Lester Young's solos, and he got himself straightened out.
